title: Directory Listing Enabled on API Endpoint
description: The API root directory at /api/ has directory listing enabled, allowing unauthenticated enumeration of all available API endpoints. The Apache web server is configured to display a directory index with file names, modification times, and sizes for all PHP files in the /api/ directory. This enables attackers to quickly discover the complete API surface without requiring traditional endpoint enumeration or reverse engineering techniques.
impact: Information disclosure allowing attackers to discover all available API endpoints without needing to perform traditional endpoint enumeration. This reduces the attack surface discovery time and reveals the complete API structure including sensitive functionality like password change and user registration endpoints. Combined with other vulnerabilities already documented (IDOR, privilege escalation, authentication bypass), this disclosure significantly accelerates exploitation of the application.
evidence:
HTTP GET request to http://localhost:8080/api/ returns HTTP 200 OK with Apache HTML directory listing containing:
- change_password.php (1.5K) - Last modified: 2025-12-02 16:09
- get_favorite_restaurants.php (1.3K) - Last modified: 2025-12-02 16:09
- login.php (800 bytes) - Last modified: 2025-12-02 16:09
- register.php (802 bytes) - Last modified: 2025-12-02 16:09
- search_restaurants.php (858 bytes) - Last modified: 2025-12-02 16:09

The response includes Apache/2.4.41 (Ubuntu) server header and complete HTML directory listing table with sortable columns (Name, Last modified, Size). All endpoints are clickable links, enabling direct access discovery. No authentication is required to enumerate the endpoints.
remediation:
1. Disable directory listing in Apache configuration by adding 'Options -Indexes' to the httpd.conf file in the VirtualHost or Directory section for /api/:
   ```
   <Directory /var/www/html/api>
       Options -Indexes
   </Directory>
   ```

2. Alternatively, create an index.html or index.php file in the /api/ directory to serve as the default response instead of showing directory contents.

3. If using .htaccess, add the following line:
   ```
   Options -Indexes
   ```

4. Restart Apache: `sudo systemctl restart apache2`

5. Verify the fix by accessing /api/ and confirming HTTP 403 Forbidden or a custom response is returned instead of directory listing.
references: CWE-548: Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing, OWASP A01:2021 Broken Access Control, CVE references for Apache directory indexing vulnerabilities
toolCallDescription: Documenting directory listing information disclosure vulnerability on /api/ endpoint with confirmed POC
